articles.title: Abbott Pays $670 Million to Settle Formula Claims as Legal Risks Persist
articles.summary: Abbott Laboratories (NYSE:ABT) has agreed to pay $670 million to settle claims involving about 2,000 people who alleged that its specialized preterm infant f...
articles.body:
Abbott Laboratories (NYSE: ABT ) has agreed to pay $670 million to settle claims involving about 2,000 people who alleged that its specialized preterm infant formulas contributed to necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), a serious and potentially fatal bowel disease affecting premature infants. The settlement also resolves Abbott's appeal of a $495 million verdict involving an Illinois mother, after that judgment was upheld by a Missouri appeals court. Abbott did not admit liability and continues to maintain that its products are safe.

The bigger issue for investors is that the settlement does not fully end the litigation. Abbott says claims from as many as 12,700 people remain, although that figure includes duplicate and unsupported claims as well as cases where it is unclear which manufacturer's formula was used. More than 825 federal cases are consolidated in Chicago, with additional cases pending in state courts.

That makes the settlement both a cost and a potential step toward reducing uncertainty around the litigation.

The strongest argument for Abbott Laboratories (NYSE:ABT) is that the $670 million settlement could put a meaningful portion of the legal risk behind the company. Rather than continuing to spend years fighting individual cases and risking additional large jury awards, Abbott has chosen to settle with a sizable group of plaintiffs. The company said the agreement is intended to substantially resolve the broader litigation.

There is also an important distinction between the products involved in the lawsuits and Abbott's broader nutrition business. The litigation concerns specialized formulas and products used for premature infants in hospitals, rather than the ordinary infant formulas sold through stores. That limits the direct exposure of Abbott's wider consumer nutrition portfolio.

Abbott Laboratories (NYSE:ABT)'s underlying business also gives investors some cushion against the settlement. The company reaffirmed its 2026 comparable sales growth guidance of 6.5% to 7.5% and raised its adjusted EPS outlook to $5.45-$5.60 after its second-quarter results. Medical Devices, Diagnostics and other businesses continue to provide growth engines outside Nutrition.

There is also evidence that the Nutrition business itself is recovering. Abbott reported that second-quarter Nutrition sales benefited from a recovery in U.S. infant-formula market share and growth in its adult nutrition business. Most importantly, the scientific and regulatory picture is not as straightforward as the lawsuits suggest. Reuters reported that U.S. regulatory agencies and an NIH-convened working group found that higher NEC rates were linked to the absence of breast milk rather than formula use. Abbott can therefore continue defending the safety of its products while settling cases for financial and strategic reasons.

articles.title: Aramco Signs $3.7 Billion in Deals With French Companies
articles.summary: Aramco is expanding its French partnerships across drilling equipment, industrial technology, and supply chain development.
articles.body:
Saudi Aramco has announced more than $3.7 billion in potential agreements with French companies as the oil giant moves to strengthen its supply chain and expand the use of artificial intelligence and other digital technologies across its operations.

The agreements and memorandum of understanding were announced during a French-Saudi investment roundtable attended by Aramco President and CEO Amin Nasser.

The package includes a corporate procurement agreement covering drilling equipment and a purchase agreement for oil country tubular goods, or OCTG, a category of steel pipe used in drilling and well construction.

Aramco Digital also signed an MoU establishing a framework for potential cooperation in industrial artificial intelligence, virtual twin and digital twin technologies, including possible applications in the oil and gas sector.

Aramco said the partnerships could improve operational continuity and efficiency while supporting technology transfer, capability development and supply chain resilience. The company did not identify the French counterparties in its announcement or disclose how the potential $3.7 billion value is divided among the individual agreements.

The initiative fits into Aramco's broader strategy of localizing and diversifying its procurement network while introducing more advanced digital technology into its upstream and downstream operations. For equipment suppliers, closer procurement relationships with one of the world's largest oil producers could provide access to significant long-term demand as Saudi Arabia continues investing across its energy and industrial sectors.

The digital component also reflects a wider industry push toward AI, predictive analytics and digital-twin systems, which energy companies are increasingly using to optimize facilities, reduce downtime and improve maintenance and production decisions.

The agreements further deepen commercial links between Saudi Arabia and France as Riyadh seeks international technology and industrial partnerships alongside its domestic economic diversification program.

articles.title: Shell’s Chemicals Exit Attracts XOM and LYB: Capital Discipline or Missed Opportunity?
articles.summary: Shell plc (NYSE:SHEL) is considering selling its U.S. chemicals business, with potential buyers including ExxonMobil, LyondellBasell, Apollo and the chemical...
articles.body:
Shell plc (NYSE: SHEL ) is considering selling its U.S. chemicals business, with potential buyers including ExxonMobil, LyondellBasell, Apollo and the chemicals arm of Kuwait Petroleum Corporation. The assets could fetch as much as $8 billion, although the bids are still non-binding and there is no guarantee a deal will happen.

The potential sale would mark a major strategic shift. Shell plc (NYSE:SHEL) has invested heavily in its chemicals operations, including $14 billion in the Monaca, Pennsylvania complex, which can produce up to 1.6 million tonnes of polymers annually. Selling the broader U.S. portfolio for up to $8 billion would therefore mean accepting a substantial discount to invested capital.

The move fits CEO Wael Sawan's broader strategy of directing capital toward businesses where Shell believes it can generate better returns. Shell has previously identified roughly $45 billion of capital in chemicals and renewables as underperforming and said it did not consider itself the "natural owner" of its chemicals portfolio.

The biggest positive for Shell plc (NYSE:SHEL) is capital discipline. Rather than continuing to pour money into a chemicals business that has historically struggled to generate attractive returns, Shell can potentially monetize the assets and redirect capital toward higher-return oil, gas and LNG opportunities. The presence of several interested buyers also gives Shell some negotiating leverage, particularly if bidders compete for the most attractive facilities.

The divestment also fits with Shell's recent earnings momentum. The company generated $9.84 billion of net profit in the second quarter of 2026, more than double the year-earlier figure and its second-highest quarterly profit on record. Strong oil and gas prices, LNG and trading activity helped drive the result, while net debt fell to $41.8 billion and gearing declined to 18.7%.

A successful chemicals sale could therefore reinforce the market's view of Shell plc (NYSE:SHEL) as a more focused energy company rather than a conglomerate spread across too many businesses. The company is already moving in this direction, including its agreement to acquire Canadian shale producer ARC Resources for $16.4 billion, its largest acquisition in a decade.

There is also a potential valuation benefit. Even though an $8 billion sale would be well below Shell's historical investment, turning an underperforming asset into cash can still be value-accretive if the proceeds are redeployed into businesses generating higher returns. For shareholders, the key question is not how much Shell originally invested, but what return the assets can generate going forward.

articles.title: TotalEnergies Navigates Hormuz Crisis with Discounted Oil and Strong Trading Economics
articles.summary: TotalEnergies SE (NYSE:TTE) is showing that its trading and integrated business model can create opportunities even in a highly disrupted oil market. CEO Pat...
articles.body:
TotalEnergies SE (NYSE: TTE ) is showing that its trading and integrated business model can create opportunities even in a highly disrupted oil market. CEO Patrick Pouyanne said the company is still profitably moving crude through the Strait of Hormuz because Middle Eastern producers are offering oil at steep discounts to compensate buyers for the risks and higher transportation costs. Crude from Iraq and Qatar is reportedly being sold for around $50-$60 a barrel, while Brent was above $90, more than offsetting the roughly $10-a-barrel additional cost of moving a VLCC through Hormuz.

The situation is particularly favorable for TotalEnergies SE (NYSE:TTE) because of its large trading operation and integrated asset base. The company has already demonstrated its ability to capitalize on Middle East market dislocations; Reuters reported that TotalEnergies made more than $1 billion from major Middle Eastern crude trades earlier this year after its traders anticipated the worsening regional situation.

At the same time, TotalEnergies recognizes that relying on Hormuz is not sustainable. The company plans to invest in alternative export infrastructure, including the Baghdad-Syria pipeline and an expansion of the UAE's Habshan-Fujairah pipeline. The existing Fujairah route can handle around 1.8 million barrels per day, with the UAE aiming to double its capacity.

The biggest bullish argument is that TotalEnergies SE (NYSE:TTE) is turning a major geopolitical disruption into a trading opportunity. While many producers and refiners are struggling with disrupted logistics, TotalEnergies' trading arm can source heavily discounted crude and still transport it profitably. A crude price of $50-$60 per barrel versus Brent above $90 creates a substantial pricing cushion, even after the additional transportation cost.

TotalEnergies' integrated business model is another advantage. The company is not simply dependent on producing oil; its trading, refining, transportation, and downstream operations give it more flexibility to exploit price dislocations across the energy market. Its earlier Middle East trading gains, which Reuters said exceeded $1 billion, provide evidence that the company can monetize volatility rather than simply suffer from it.

There is also a potential downstream benefit. While crude is moving through Hormuz at discounted prices, refined products are facing much higher transportation costs, with Pouyanne estimating an additional $50 per barrel in some cases. That has created shortages of refined products and a much stronger products market. For an integrated energy company such as TotalEnergies, stronger refining margins could help offset pressure elsewhere in the business.

articles.title: 'Shark Tank' star Daniel Lubetzky shares 3 steps to turn a wild idea into a viable business
articles.summary: Kind Snacks founder and "Shark Tank" star Daniel Lubetzky says the best business ideas often begin by sounding ridiculous.
articles.body:
Some of the world's wildest ideas sounded implausible before becoming huge businesses.

Daniel Lubetzky told Business Insider that founders shouldn't dismiss those ideas too soon.

The "Shark Tank" investor shares his 3-step method for moving an idea toward reality.

Daniel Lubetzky knows firsthand that great business ideas can sound far-fetched at first.

But the "Shark Tank" investor and Kind Snacks founder says entrepreneurs should not dismiss their most outlandish ideas too soon because they're the ones that can turn into some of the most successful businesses.

"Out of those crazy things — that's when the Kind bar comes out, the Ring machine that Jamie Siminoff invented — it has to come from the thinking outside of pushing yourself," he said, citing his company's Kind snack bar and the smart-doorbell company acquired by Amazon in 2018 for about $1 billion.

The business world is littered with such examples. Airbnb cofounder and CEO Brian Chesky has said people thought it was " crazy " to imagine strangers staying in one another's homes. And Spotify founder Daniel Ek has described the company's original aim — making every song instantly and legally available — as an " impossible idea ."

Ahead of the launch of his "Build or Break" podcast on September 3, Lubetzky shared with Business Insider his three-part framework for turning any business idea — no matter how bizarre — from a brainstorm into reality.

"When you're brainstorming, you have to only brainstorm," Lubetzky said. "You have to not allow any filters to apply because it's almost like you need to be looking for the stupidest idea."

He said founders should push beyond the obvious options and put every idea on the board, however unrealistic it may initially appear. The goal is to escape conventional thinking , because that is where original concepts can emerge.

"The crazier you go, the more you put on your board," he said. "You cannot filter anything out because you have to push yourself outside of that box for you to come up with something that nobody else has ever come up with."

After stepping away from the brainstorm, founders should interrogate the ideas that remain with discipline, Lubetzky said.

They should consider whether they have the necessary skills, whether customers want the product, whether the economics work, and whether competitors could do it better.

"You take a break and then you start applying all of the filters," he said. "Do I have what it takes to do this? Are these the skills that are necessary, and do I have all those skills? Is the input-to-output correlation worth it? Does the consumer really want it? Is there no other competition that can do it better?"

articles.title: United Airlines' Relax Row turns 3 economy seats into a couch — and one plus-size traveler says it's a game-changer
articles.summary: More space could make long-haul flights easier — if the price is right.
articles.body:
Flying can be an uncomfortable experience for just about anyone. But for plus-size travelers, there can be an added layer of stress before the flight even begins. A cramped seat, limited legroom, and hours spent shoulder-to-shoulder with a complete stranger can make a long flight especially difficult.

Travel journalist and author Robin Raven knows that experience firsthand. In a recent piece for Yahoo , Raven wrote about the realities of flying as a plus-size traveler — and why United Airlines' upcoming economy seating option caught her attention.

Raven wrote that she'd "absolutely" pay extra for a flight that's free of concerns about being "elbowed and squished."

That's because United is working on something economy passengers don't typically get: a row of seats that can turn into a couch.

United is turning three economy seats into a couch

The airline is calling it the Relax Row, and the concept is straightforward.

Three economy seats are fitted with leg rests that can be raised after takeoff, creating a larger, lie-flat surface across the row. So instead of trying to sleep sitting upright, passengers can stretch out across the seats.

The airline is also adding a few extras to make the setup feel more like a bed. Passengers will get a custom-fitted mattress pad, a specially sized blanket, and two additional pillows. Families using the Relax Row will also get a stuffed toy and a children's travel kit.

The seats will sit between United Economy and United Premium Plus, giving passengers another option if a standard economy seat isn't cutting it but a premium cabin feels like too much of a hit to the wallet.

However, the changes aren't immediate. United expects to launch the Relax Row in 2027, starting with its Boeing 787 and 777 wide-body aircraft. The airline says it plans to have the option on more than 200 of those planes by 2030, with as many as 12 Relax Row sections on a plane .

Where to find the best savings interest rates today

The average interest rate on a traditional savings account is only 0.38%, according to the FDIC. However, today's best high-yield savings accounts pay around 3%-4%.

How much interest can I earn with a high-yield savings account?

The amount of interest you can earn from a savings account depends on the annual percentage rate (APY). This is a measure of your total earnings after one year when considering the base interest rate and how often interest compounds (savings account interest typically compounds daily).

Say you put $1,000 in a savings account at the average interest rate of 0.38% with daily compounding. At the end of one year, your balance would grow to $1,003.81 — your initial $1,000 deposit, plus just $3.81 in interest.

Now, let's say you choose a high-yield savings account that offers 4% APY instead. In this case, your balance would grow to $1,040.81 over the same period, which includes $40.81 in interest.

The more you deposit in an HYSA, the more you stand to earn. If we took our same example of a high-yield savings account at 4% APY, but deposited $10,000, your total balance after one year would be $10,408.08, meaning you'd earn $408.08 in interest. ​​

Deposit account rates — including savings rates — are tied to the federal funds rate . This is the target interest rate set by the Federal Reserve; when it increases its target rate, deposit account rates usually increase. Conversely, when the Fed lowers its rate, deposit rates fall.

Savings account interest rates have fluctuated quite a bit over the past couple of decades. From 2010 to about 2015, rates were rock-bottom, hovering between 0.06% and 0.10%. This was largely due to the 2008 financial crisis​ and the Federal Reserve 's decision to lower its target rate to near zero in order to spur economic growth.

From 2015 to 2018, interest rates gradually increased. However, they remained low by historical standards. Then, the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 led to another sharp decrease in rates as the Fed cut rates again to stimulate the economy. This brought average savings interest rates down to new lows, around 0.05% to 0.06%, by mid-2021.

Since then, savings account rates have recovered considerably, largely driven by the Fed's interest rate hikes in response to skyrocketing inflation. However, the Fed finally lowered the federal funds rate toward the end of 2024 and continued to do so throughout 2025. As a result, deposit rates have steadily declined. Is now a good time to put your money in a high-yield savings account?

Choosing where to put your money is an important decision, and there are a few factors you should consider when evaluating your options. A high-yield savings account could make sense if you're looking for a secure place to hold shorter-term savings while earning a solid return.

Interest rates: One of the most important features of a savings account is the interest rate. It's important to shop around and compare the best offers to ensure your money will grow over time. Considering that savings rates will likely drop in the near future, opening a high-yield savings account now will allow you to take advantage of historically high rates.

Goals: Today's high-yield savings accounts offer rates we haven't seen in more than a decade. That said, savings rates still don't match average returns for the stock market. If you're saving for a long-term goal like retirement, a savings account probably isn't the best place to put your money, since your balance won't grow at a pace that will allow you to reach your target. However, if you're saving for a financial emergency, a down payment on a home or car, holiday gifts, or another short-term goal, a savings account is a great place to hold those funds.

Accessibility: Certain types of accounts and investments may provide higher returns than a savings account, but may make it difficult to access your funds in a pinch. For example, if you put your savings in a certificate of deposit (CD) and need to access the money before the maturity date, you could be subject to an early withdrawal penalty. So, if you want to be able to dip into your savings as needed, a high-yield savings account is likely the better choice.

Security: In most cases, savings accounts are insured by the FDIC up to the federal limit. They also can't lose money due to fluctuations in the market, making them a low-risk option.

Do online banks have the best savings account rates?

Online banks operate exclusively via the web. This significantly reduces their overhead costs, so they're able to pass those savings onto customers in the form of high deposit rates and low fees. In fact, many of the best high-yield savings accounts also come with zero monthly fees or minimum opening deposit requirements. If you're searching for the best savings interest rates, online banks are a great place to start .

That said, online banks aren't the only place you can find savings accounts with rates that range between 3% and 4% APY. Credit unions are not-for-profit financial cooperatives known for offering competitive rates and fewer fees. Many credit unions have requirements that must be met to become a member, though some allow just about anyone to join.

How to open a high-yield savings account

The requirements involved in opening a savings account vary by financial institution. However, if you're ready to open an account, you can follow these general steps:

Research savings account rates: Of course, when choosing a savings account, one of the most important factors to evaluate is the interest rate. Be sure that you select a savings account with a competitive rate to help your money grow.

Figure out your must-haves: Although savings account interest rates should be top of mind, that's not the only factor to consider. You'll also want to think about what else you need from your account, whether it's no minimum-balance requirement , low fees, or other perks. Finding a savings account with a solid rate that also helps you achieve your goals is key.

Prepare documentation: Opening a bank account requires you to provide a few important personal details and documents. Before you start your application, be sure you have your Social Security number, driver's license or passport number, and proof of address.

Fill out the application: In many cases, you can apply for a savings account online. However, some financial institutions may require you to visit the branch in person to apply. Either way, the application for a new savings account should only take a few minutes to complete. In many cases, you'll get your approval decision instantly.

Fund your account: Once your savings account application is approved, you'll need to add funds to the account. Be sure you're aware of any minimum opening deposit requirements and the timeline for funding.

Is a high-yield savings account right for you?

A high-yield savings account is a good fit if you want to earn a competitive return on money you'll need in the near future while keeping it safe and accessible. It's important to not only consider whether the interest rate is attractive, but whether the account matches the purpose of your savings.

You want to maximize your emergency fund.

You're saving for a goal within the next one to five years.

You have extra cash sitting in a low-interest checking or traditional savings account.

You prioritize safety over higher potential investment returns.

You don't need to write checks or use the money for everyday spending.

An HYSA may not be the best choice if...

You're investing for retirement or another goal that's 10+ years away. Investing in a diversified portfolio has historically produced higher long-term returns, though with greater risk.

You won't need the money for a fixed period. If you can leave your savings untouched for several months or years, a certificate of deposit (CD) may offer a higher guaranteed yield.

You need frequent access to your money. A checking account is more convenient for paying bills and making everyday purchases.

articles.title: Fire kills 14 newborns at major hospital in Pakistan, officials say
articles.summary: Poor enforcement of building safety regulations in Pakistan has been blamed for the high death toll in fires.
articles.body:
A fire at a hospital's maternity ward in a major government hospital in Pakistan's capital killed at least 14 newborn babies early on Wednesday, according to hospital officials and the government.

The fire broke out on the third floor of the Mother and Child Health Ward at the public Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) hospital, according to the district administration.

Rescue officials said the fire broke out at around 6:45 am (3:45 am CEST) after an air-conditioning unit compressor apparently exploded inside the nursery, located in the hospital's gynecology ward.

Sohail Ashraf, the Islamabad chief commissioner, said on X that rescue teams, specialists, police and himself "immediately reached at site and controlled the fire."

At least one baby was reportedly rescued.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed sorrow over the deaths and ordered an immediate investigation.

"The loss of children in such circumstances is irreparable," a statement from his office said.

Sharif also expressed his "heartfelt condolences to the families of the innocent children," adding that he was "saddened by this tragic incident.".

Police said the newborns killed in the fire were severely burned, making DNA testing necessary to confirm their identities before their bodies can be released to their families.

The statement came after parents called for the bodies to be handed over immediately.

Fires in large buildings are frequent in Pakistan, often due to poor safety laws and building codes as well as lax enforcement.

articles.title: Tanzania's vice president resigns in test to the country's democracy
articles.summary: Tanzania’s vice president is resigning after less than a year in office, following what analysts say was a power struggle with the country’s first female lea...
articles.body:
KAMPALA, Uganda (AP) — Tanzania's vice president is resigning after less than a year in office, following what analysts say was a power struggle with the country's first female leader.

Vice President Emmanuel Nchimbi offered to vacate the office on Sept. 4, according to a statement released on Tuesday. The presidency confirmed that constitutional measures will be taken to select a new deputy to President Samia Suluhu Hassan .

Nchimbi's statement said he was "fully convinced" that Hassan desires another deputy. "I assure you that I will continue to be a good citizen of Tanzania," it said.

His resignation is remarkable in a country known for its relative stability under the one-party rule of the Chama cha Mapinduzi party, or CCM.

Some analysts say he appeared to have disagreed with Hassan over governance and other issues stemming from the government's brutal crackdown on street protests during and after the Oct. 29 election.

"The two were not on good terms," said Tito Magoti, a rights attorney and independent analyst in the commercial capital of Dar es Salaam.

A postelection inquiry showed 518 people were killed in the violence, shocking many at home and abroad . The military was deployed alongside the police to quell riots in major cities, with sporadic gunfire ringing out in the usually peaceful country that many foreigners visit for its pristine coastal beaches and safari tourism.

The internet was shut down for days, a move that Hassan later apologized for and promised would never happen again.

The leader of the commission that investigated election-related violence, Mohamed Chande Othman, said during the release of his report in April that the number of deaths was likely higher, because some families buried their loved ones without taking their bodies to morgues. He recommended an investigation into the use of firearms, as some of the witnesses told the commission that their loved ones were shot while sitting inside their houses.

Hassan, who has served as president since 2021, drew widespread anger for running virtually unopposed after her two main opponents were blocked or prevented from contesting. Her main rival, Tundu Lissu , is currently jailed over treason charges he says are politically motivated.

A version of CCM has ruled Tanzania since the country gained independence from Britain in 1961. CCM is fused with the state and effectively in charge of the security apparatus.

Hassan, who was formerly a vice president, became president without incident when her predecessor, John Pombe Magufuli, died suddenly after the start of his second term.

The orderly transition sustained Tanzania's reputation as an oasis of political stability and relative peace, a major reason for CCM's considerable support, especially among rural voters.

___ An Associated Press reporter in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, contributed to this report.

articles.title: Phillies Get Ketel Marte Update After Viral Casino Incident
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Phillies received some unfortunate news around the Arizona Diamondbacks superstar shortly after a head-turning decision.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Phillies have little room for error as they chase down the Atlanta Braves in the National League East, with every remaining series carrying significant postseason implications.

Philadelphia has surged at exactly the right time. The Phillies entered the final weeks of the regular season riding a nine-game winning streak and, even though that came to an end on Monday against the Seattle Mariners , that surge dramatically tightening the division race while also strengthening the team's position in the NL Wild Card picture.

"The Atlanta Braves saw their lead in the NL East whittled down to three games by the red-hot Philadelphia Phillies, potentially setting the stage for a competitive division race we didn't think we'd have down the stretch," Steve Gardner wrote for USA Today . "On the wave of their current nine-game winning streak, the Phils dramatically improved their playoff position over the past week, gaining serious ground on the Braves and moving into the NL's second wild-card spot with five weeks remaining in the regular season."

That makes Philadelphia's upcoming series in Arizona particularly interesting, especially with Diamondbacks star Ketel Marte set to return in time to challenge the Phillies ascension in the standings.

Philadelphia Phillies Get Unfortunate Ketel Marte Update Before Arizona Diamondbacks Series

Marte has been at the center of an unusual saga, which began with an unexplained absence before a matchup with the Boston Red Sox and escalated after he was spotted at a casino.

"The Ketel Marte saga took another turn Friday as photos surfaced on social media showing the Diamondbacks second baseman at a local casino during the team's home game against the Reds ," Mike Axisa reported for CBS Sports . "Marte is currently on the injured list with a knee issue. He was initially placed on the restricted list after failing to show up for a game against the Red Sox in Boston on Monday."

Though Marte went viral for spending his recovery time at a casino after leaving his team, the Diamondbacks have indicated that he will be welcomed back to the lineup when he's healthy. And the Phillies have no learned they can expect that return to come when they face the Diamondbacks at the start of next week.

"Ketel Marte is tentatively expected to be activated next Tuesday, when the D-backs open their series against the Phillies in Arizona," MLB insider Francys Romero reported on X . "The infielder began his knee rehab last Friday in Arizona, putting him on track for a potential return."

The timing adds an extra challenge for a Phillies team looking to make up some ground in the division race with time running out.

Philadelphia Phillies Get Ketel Marte Update At Critical Juncture

Marte's potential return would give the Diamondbacks one of its most accomplished players back in the lineup, even if some teammates hold hard feelings over his sudden disappearance. He finished third in NL MVP voting in 2024 and has made an All-Star and won a Silver Slugger Award in both 2024 and 2025.

For the Phillies, the objective is straightforward: keep winning and put pressure on Atlanta. But the upcoming trip to Arizona could present an additional challenge if Marte does return as expected.

articles.summary: The pair made a strong start by taking the opening set but Henry Patten and doubles specialist Katerina Siniakova hit back to claim the second before dominat...
articles.body:
Like this article? Keep independent journalism alive. Support HuffPost .

NEW YORK, Aug 25 (Reuters) - Top seeds Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka suffered an early exit from the U.S. Open mixed doubles on Tuesday, falling 1-4 4-2 10-2 to Henry Patten and Katerina Siniakova in their opening match.

Djokovic, a 24-times Grand Slam singles champion, and four-times major winner Sabalenka made a strong start by taking the opening set. But Patten and doubles specialist Siniakova hit back to claim the second before dominating the tiebreak to secure a place in the quarter-finals.

Siniakova sealed the upset in style with an ace out wide on match point, ending the tournament hopes of the star-studded pairing.

"It wasn't looking very good for a while, in this format we play one bad game and all of a sudden the first set's gone," Patten said.

"We knew the same could happen in the second, and we played an amazing tiebreak. Kat acing Novak on match point was great."

The mixed doubles championship is once again being staged in the week before the singles main draw, after organisers revamped the format last year to attract more leading singles players by reducing the field and giving the event a standalone slot on the calendar.

The revamped format proved a commercial success in its debut year, drawing sellout crowds and attracting many of the sport's biggest singles names despite criticism from some doubles specialists, who argued it marginalised established pairings.

Italian duo Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori went on to retain the title by defeating Iga Swiatek and Casper Ruud in last year's final.

(Reporting by Pearl Josephine Nazare in Bengaluru; Editing by Toby Davis)

ESPN's Mike Clay recently came out with his annual positional rankings ahead of the 2026 season. Clay doesn't think much of the Washington Commanders , with Washington falling to the bottom of the rankings at every position except quarterback, and receiving an overall rating of No. 24.

Washington's highest ranking was quarterback at No. 8. This is not surprising given the promise surrounding quarterback Jayden Daniels . They also have a solid backup in Marcus Mariota . So it is understandable why the Commanders' quarterback room ranks in the top 10 in the league.

Lowest Rankings - Running Back (No. 31) and Offensive Line (No. 31)

Both the Commanders running back room and offensive line room were ranked next-to-last. This ranking for the running back room is not exactly surprising. Washington had one of the best rushing offenses in the NFL last season, finishing in the top-five in rushing yards and top-10 in rushing touchdowns. Even with their rushing success last season, they decided to add a new backup in Rachaad White . Jacory Croskey-Merritt , who led Washington in rushing yards last season, will remain the top back. Croskey-Merritt and White are not the most well-known running backs in the NFL, but they should certainly be a productive duo given Washington's success in the run game last season. Therefore, Clay's rankings of the Commanders' running backs seem rather inaccurate.

His ranking of the offensive line, however, is in line with some other websites, such as Pro Football Focus , which ranked Washington's offensive line as the worst in the league due to the loss of left tackle Laremy Tunsil Jr for the majority of the season. There have also been injury concerns with the Commanders' center, Nick Allegretti , throughout training camp. Unless Washington adds depth to the offensive line before the season begins, this unit could really struggle.

Most Surprising Ranking - Wide Receiver (No. 22)

Besides the low ranking for the running back room, the ranking for the wide receiver group is also shocking. Washington had one of the worst passing offenses last season, but that is partly because Jayden Daniels and top wide receiver Terry McLaurin were out most of the season. Deebo Samuel led the Commanders in receiving last season, and while he is gone, Washington still has McLaurin; they signed Stefon Diggs and drafted promising rookie Antonio Williams . Depth receiver Luke McCaffrey is also still on the roster. There are concerns about McLaurin's and Diggs' ages because they are both in their 30s. However, that doesn't seem relevant, since both are still elite receivers in this league.

Also, when you look at the teams ahead of Washington, not all of them have better wide receivers than the Commanders. For example, the Arizona Cardinals ' wide receivers rank above Washington's. Their leading receiver last season was a tight end; their top receiver on the roster is Marvin Harrison Jr who has yet to live up to his expectations coming out of college. So, looking at the rankings, ranking Washington's receivers at No. 22 in the league does not make sense.

Saying Washington is going to be one of the worst teams in the league seems shocking. Among the teams ranked ahead of the Commanders are the New York Jets , who do not even have a solid quarterback situation. Washington is also ranked the lowest of any team in the NFC East, with the Philadelphia Eagles at No. 3, the Dallas Cowboys at No. 9, and the New York Giants at No. 23. This is a team that made the NFC Championship in 2024, and they have some key pieces from that 2024 team. The Commanders shouldn't be in the bottom half of the league or last in their division.

articles.title: Israel's seizure of Unrwa training college in East Jerusalem condemned
articles.summary: It marks the shutting of the last of the Palestinian refugee agency's facilities in the sector of the city, after Israel passed a law against it.
articles.body:
Israeli security forces have seized and closed a training college run by the UN agency for Palestinian refugees (Unrwa), the last of its facilities that was still operating in occupied East Jerusalem.

UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres has condemned the incursion of the Qalandia Training Centre, the latest move to threaten Unrwa after Israel passed laws against it.

His spokesman, Stephane Dujarric, said that under international law, all UN premises "are inviolable and immune from any form of interference."

Israel's far-right National Security Minister, Itamar Ben-Gvir, joined the large raid on Tuesday and released a video of himself in the chair of the director of the Unrwa institute.

The office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he had given the directive for the evacuation of the Unrwa compound, accusing the agency of involvement in the deadly Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, which it strongly denies.

The Qalandia Training Centre, which was set up in 1952, trained some 340 Palestinians a year in valuable vocational skills including carpentry, car mechanics and plumbing.

Although the site is in East Jerusalem, its location between Qalandia and Kfar Aqab is behind Israel's separation barrier, which made it accessible to young people from refugee camps across the West Bank.

Staff have been expelled from the college. The Israeli authorities say equipment is being removed from the site, and they intend to turn part of it into a school.

In a statement, Unrwa said it "unequivocally condemns this unauthorised and deeply concerning incursion into the Qalandia Training Centre".

"The entry of armed security forces into a United Nations facility, without the authorisation or consent of the United Nations, is unacceptable."

Israeli legislation, which came into force last year, banned Unrwa from carrying out missions or operating within what Israel deemed to be its territory. This includes East Jerusalem, which was captured by Israel from Jordan in the 1967 Middle East War and later annexed in a move that is not recognised by most countries.

All Israeli state authorities were also banned from having contact with Unrwa.

Closure orders were issued last year for six Unrwa schools in East Jerusalem, ending in-person teaching for some 800 Palestinian children.

Following the raid on Qalandia Training College, the UN's spokesman said: "The secretary general is greatly alarmed at this development, as it will deprive young people of the vocational education they were receiving."

Israel's security minister made a point of publicising the action, taking a TV crew from pro-government Channel 14 with him for the raid.

"Thank God, on my shift there is no Unrwa, there is no management, they will not be here," Ben-Gvir said in his video at the college.

Moves against Unrwa are broadly popular in Israel and the prime minister put out a statement highlighting his responsibility.

"In accordance with my instructions and in furtherance of the law we passed, the evacuation of the Unrwa compound in Kafr Aqab, Jerusalem, began today," Netanyahu said.

"The State of Israel will not allow an organisation whose employees were involved in terrorism and the October 7 massacre to operate on its territory and will use all means necessary to act against it," he added.

Israeli intelligence claimed that at least 19 Unrwa employees took part in the 7 October cross-border attack on southern Israel, which killed some 1,200 people and led to the abduction of 251 hostages. A UN investigation found that in nine cases the evidence indicated possible involvement, so their contracts were terminated. It found insufficient or no evidence to support claims in the other cases.

Israel further alleged that 10 per cent of Unrwa's Gaza employees had active links to Palestinian armed groups and that Unrwa facilities were used for Hamas military purposes. Unrwa says it has never been given information or evidence from the Israeli authorities about the former allegation and that it has systematically condemned any violations of UN premises which violate their neutrality.

The Palestinian Authority's ministry of foreign affairs called on the international community to "take immediate and effective measures" to protect the college and "ensure the return of its personnel and prevent Israel from turning this assault into a permanent fait accompli".

Unrwa was first set up to support Palestinians who fled or were expelled from their land in fighting before and after the state of Israel was created in 1948.

Many Palestinians see Israeli attacks on the agency as an attempt to dispense with the issue of Palestinian refugees and their "right to return" to their historic homes and property, which is a core issue in the Israel-Palestinian conflict.

articles.title: Colts' cornerback unit receives top 10 ranking entering 2026 season
articles.summary: In ESPN's most recent positional rankings, the Indianapolis Colts cornerback room, led by All-Pro Sauce Gardner, ranked No. 8 in the NFL.
articles.body:
When you think of the 2026 Indianapolis Colts , running back Jonathan Taylor is probably one of the first players that comes to mind. Another player that could come to mind is cornerback Sauce Gardner .

Although the All-Pro only played four games with the Colts last season after being traded from the New York Jets halfway through the year, he is one of the most talented players on Indianapolis' roster.

Gardner is probably a big reason why ESPN 's Mike Clay ranked the Colts cornerback room as a top 10 unit, coming in at No. 8 overall. There are only four teams in the AFC that are ahead of Indianapolis in the cornerback rankings, including their AFC South rival, the Houston Texans , who came in first.

Last season, the Colts gave up the second-most passing yards out of any team in the league, although they were top-10 in interceptions, as the cornerback room navigated injuries.

But when healthy, this could be one of the best starting units in football.

On the opposite side of Gardner is Charvarius Ward , who is going into his second season with Indianapolis. However, he only played seven games with the Colts last year due to injuries, although he was still quite impactful when on the field, allowing a completion rate of just 56% when targeted.

Ward's best season was back in 2024 when he was a Pro-Bowler and second-team All-Pro. That season, he recorded five interceptions and defended 23 total passes.

Overall, Indianapolis should live up to its top-10 ranking at cornerback as long as Gardner and Ward stay healthy.

articles.title: Youngsters 'not ready' says Watford boss Dionisi
articles.summary: Watford boss Alessio Dionisi made 11 changes only to watch his young side be dumped out of the Carabao Cup by Peterborough.
articles.body:
Watford boss Alessio Dionisi admits his young players are not yet ready for the first-team after their humbling defeat by League One side Peterborough United in the Carabao Cup.

The Posh ran riot in a 5-1 thrashing at Vicarage Road against a youthful Hornets side after Watford made a promising start to the league campaign under new head coach Dionisi, picking up four points in the first two games.

"I'm not happy, we're not happy but this is football. Yesterday, the young boys worked well [in training] but the official match is different," Dionisi told BBC Three Counties Radio.

"For them, it is difficult because [they] are not ready to stay in the first-team but, for me, it's not a problem. It is important for everyone to prepare for the next match against West Ham because it will be very, very difficult for us."

Dionisi made 11 changes from the side that started Saturday's Championship 1-1 draw at Wrexham , naming two 17-year-old's and eight players under the age of 20 as his side were comprehensively dumped out of the cup in the second round.

"I am sorry for our supporters but, for me, there wasn't another possibility for us to play every three days with the same line-up. It is impossible," said Dionisi.

"The result is terrible but, in this moment, we prefer to choose to prepare [for] the Championship [over the Carabao Cup].

"We need new players to complete this team. We need new players with experience but we will work with what we have."

articles.title: Max Verstappen theories over new F1 contract dismissed by Red Bull boss
articles.summary: Verstappen signed a contract extension until 2030 after being strongly linked with a move to Mercedes or McLaren
articles.body:
Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies quickly shut down two theories about Max Verstappen 's contract extension that were put forward by Nico Rosberg .

Four-time F1 world champion Verstappen signed a new contract with Red Bull until 2030 last week, which will extend the Dutch driver's partnership with the team to 15 years if he sees out his deal.

Rosberg, the world champion in Verstappen's debut Red Bull year in 2016, was in conversation with Mekies on the grid at the Dutch Grand Prix in Zandvoort when he put the 28-year-old's extension down to two reasons: a reported $80m-a-year deal and the culture Mekies has installed at the team since taking over from Christian Horner last year.

Yet in response, Mekies said: "So, both statements are not correct. It's down really to the trust that Max has in the 2,000 people we have in Milton Keynes [Red Bul HQ], chassis side, PU [power unit] side, and he knows what our people are capable of and he has chosen to put his trust in us for the future.

"So, we will try to pay him back for that. He's much more than just the fastest driver in the world for us and we'll try to make sure we give him a fast car as soon as possible."

Verstappen's future was shrouded in uncertainty given his dissatisfaction with this generation of car, alongside interest from Mercedes and McLaren, but the Dutchman has opted to remain with the only team he's ever known.

"It's phenomenal news, for the team of course, but also for us as a sport as a whole," Mekies added.

"It has been a great few weeks of discussions. From day one, Max said, 'I want to stay with you guys.' When we finally concluded everything, I said, 'Well, I thought you always wanted to stay anyway!'

"Jokes aside, we take the trust he is putting in us very, very seriously. It gives us a huge responsibility in terms of providing him with a package that he will need to fight for wins again.

"But there is nothing that we want more at Red Bull Racing than to come back to the top spot as soon as possible and we know that is also what Max wants."

Verstappen will be looking to bounce back following his massive first-lap crash at the Dutch Grand Prix at the next round in Monza (6 September).

articles.title: Are you concerned by Man City 'fire sale'?
articles.summary: City boss Enzo Maresca made it quite clear during Friday's pre-match news conference that any player that is unhappy at the club is free to leave.  Maresca r...
articles.body:
Some of you have been sending questions in and Mathew asked me if Manchester City are having a "fire sale" and if the club are "tightening their belt for a specific reason".

City boss Enzo Maresca made it quite clear during Friday's pre-match news conference that any player that is unhappy at the club is free to leave.

Maresca revealed that Savio had said "from day one" that he wanted to move, while Omar Marmoush has been unhappy with the amount of gametime he has had since his move from Eintracht Frankfurt . He is too good a player to be playing second fiddle to Erling Haaland .

Are you concerned with the exits? Tell us

Tijjani Reijnders and Nico Gonzalez have both failed to nail down first-team places and the club stance has always been, if a bid comes in that matches the valuation of a player, they are free to go if they wish.

City bought Reijnders for £46.5m last summer and made a £6.5m profit on him, while they recouped most of what they paid for Gonzalez last January.

Elliot Anderson has already come in, a deal has been agreed for both Ayyoub Bouaddi and Allan Elias, while speculation around signing Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea has not gone away.

I'm expecting City and director of football Hugo Viana to do some deals before the end of the transfer window.

articles.summary: Manchester City have signed teenage Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in a five-year deal the French club said Wednesday was worth 100 million eur...
articles.body:
Manchester City have signed teenage Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in a five-year deal the French club said Wednesday was worth 100 million euros (£86 million, $117 million).

City moved for Bouaddi after selling Spain's World Cup winning captain Rodri to Barcelona and Tijjani Reijnders to Al-Qadsiah, with Nico Gonzalez also poised to leave the Etihad.

The 18-year-old rising star was one of the stand-out players at the recent World Cup, helping Morocco reach the quarter-finals before they were beaten by France.

articles.summary: Manchester City complete the signing of Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in a £85.6m deal on a five-year contract.
articles.body:
Manchester City have signed Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in a £85.6m deal.

The 18-year-old joins on a five-year contract, subject to international clearance, with City paying £81.4m upfront plus £4.2m in add-ons.

Enzo Maresca's side moved to sign Bouaddi after selling central midfielders Rodri to Barcelona in a £65m deal and Tijjani Reinders to Al-Qadsiah for £52m.

He impressed at this summer's World Cup - starting five of Morocco's six matches in their run to the quarter-finals - after becoming a key member of Lille's side in Ligue 1.

"This is a very special day for me and my family. Manchester City are, for me, the best club in the world. It's a dream to be here and be able to call myself a City player," said Bouaddi.

"I have spent most of my life working hard to become the best player I can be and reach the top of the game.

"I've watched City for many years, and I love their style of play. City always try and play quality football. And they have shown they are winners - this club feels like it's built to win."

Bouaddi made 96 appearances for Lille after making his debut in 2023, helping them finish third in Ligue 1 last season.

At the age of 16 he became the youngest footballer to ever play for the French side on his senior debut against Faroese club KI in the Europa League, before announcing himself on the world stage by playing a starring role in Lille's Champions League victory over Real Madrid in 2024.

Bouaddi will form part of a revamped midfield, with City already bringing in England midfielder Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116m.

Bouaddi functions as a deep-lying conductor and would complement Anderson, who is comfortable as a box-to-box midfielder as well as the number six role he plays for England .

City are also set to make an offer for Chelsea 's Argentina midfielder Enzo Fernandez but it remains to be seen whether a deal can be struck with the 25-year-old valued at £120m.

Bouaddi's signing comes after Brazilian winger Savinho , now known as Savio, joined Tottenham in a £75m deal earlier this week.

Spurs have also agreed a loan deal to sign City's Egypt forward Omar Marmoush , while Spain midfielder Nico Gonzalez is set to leave Maresca's side to join Newcastle in a £52m deal.

articles.title: Lake Travis, Vandegrift top our Class 6A rankings as we preview Central Texas high school football
articles.summary: Our 2026 high school football previews and district predictions for Class 6A include our first top-five rankings of the season, led by Lake Travis.
articles.body:
The American-Statesman takes a look at Class 6A districts around Central Texas as the high school football season gets underway.

Fab Five: Central Texas' top 5 teams from Class 6A

1. Lake Travis (14-1 last year, DI state semifinalist): The Cavs graduated 18 starters, but there's never a lack of talent. DBs Luca Antoun and Jeremiah Strong and LB Owen Aird lead what should be one of the area's best defenses.

This video created with the assistance of AI.

2. Vandegrift (12-2, DII state semifinalist): New QB Gavin Koester paces an offense that should thrive running the ball, and the Vipers are deep with talent at all three levels on defense.

3. Westlake (7-4, DII area round): There are more question marks than in the past decade for the Chaps. But like Lake Travis, Westlake always has talent. Wylie Nichols is one of Central Texas' better defensive backs.

4. Dripping Springs (12-2, DII regional finalist): Chase Ames is the area's most prolific 6A QB and has a massive offensive line to protect him. The Tigers seem primed for another double-digit win season.

5. Hutto (9-3, DI area round): WR/DB Jaiden Fields is one of the area's top three players. If the Hippos get good play from a new quarterback, the sky's the limit for the offense.

Our other playoff teams: Hutto, Cedar Park and East View

Notes: Cedar Park, East View, Leander and Rouse all make the jump to 6A, with Vista Ridge the district's seventh team. This district is also in Region III, which offers a much tougher playoff route than Region IV. … While Vandegrift and Hutto seem to be a level above the rest of the district, the battle for the last two playoff spots should be fierce. … Keep an eye on whether or not Vista Ridge makes the playoffs. If it does, along with Vandegrift, Cedar Park and Hutto, that would push the Vipers into DII. … East View safety Jalani Culpepper is receiving Power Four interest. … Cedar Park's David Cooper is the district's only returning starting QB. He threw for 1,925 yards and 19 TDs in 2025. … Hutto (Casey Walraven), Rouse (Mark Hopkins) and Leander (Ahmad Zaidan) all have new coaches.

Our other playoff teams: Westlake, Round Rock and Cedar Ridge

Key game: Lake Travis vs. Westlake (Oct. 23)

Notes: Westlake and Lake Travis move into a district with the five Round Rock ISD schools. … Westlake's Jackson Cook and Lake Travis' Jackson Koeppel are arguably the two best offensive linemen in Central Texas, with Cook committed to Texas. … Round Rock has something neither Westlake nor Lake Travis do: an experienced starter at quarterback. Dov Stickler returns after throwing for 1,850 yards and 15 TDs during the Dragons' final eight games. He also has one of the area's top WRs in TCU commit Dylan Jaeger. … Stony Point has a new coach in Dustin Pleasant after longtime coach Craig Chessher retired . … Cedar Ridge is looking for its first playoff appearance since 2022 and first winning season since 2021. QB Dylan Snoga accounted for 1,736 yards and 17 TDs as a junior. … Jerry Gardner is McNeil's new coach. … Westlake would need either Lake Travis or Round Rock to miss the playoffs to be in DI in the postseason.

Our other playoff teams: Bowie, Johnson and Hays

Key game: Dripping Springs vs. Bowie (Oct. 16)

Notes: Realignment strangely didn't put Dripping Springs in a district with nearby Lake Travis and Westlake, instead grouping the Tigers with fellow Hays County schools Johnson and Hays, Austin ISD's three 6A schools (Austin High, Bowie and Akins) and Del Valle. Hays moves up from 5A DI and Johnson returns to an Austin-centric district after playing south the last two years. … Dripping Springs is the overwhelming favorite, but don't count out Bowie. The Bulldogs return eight defensive starters and have a powerhouse RB in Rhys Moreno. … Johnson is the district's wildcard. The Jaguars missed the playoffs a year ago but welcome back QB Jonah Montgomery and eight other starters. … Austin High LB Ethan Kahle is arguably the best player the Central Texas public isn't aware of. He tallied 121 tackles in 2025 and leads the Maroons' hopes to reach the postseason. … Keep an eye on Hays RB Eyan Stigall. Hawks coach Mark Torres is high on his talent, and Stigall ran for 537 yards and seven TDs as a sophomore. … A DII regional final between Dripping Springs and Westlake seems likely.

articles.title: Man City complete record £86m deal for Rodri replacement
articles.summary: The Morocco international shone for Lille last term and continued his impressive run of form at the World Cup, with the 18-year-old now a key piece in the Ci...
articles.body:
Manchester City have signed Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille for £85m in a record deal for a teenager in Premier League history.

Bouaddi has signed a five-year contract at the Etihad Stadium, becomes their second midfield signing of the summer after Elliot Anderson .

City's midfield revamp has now cost over £200m – with Anderson a club record purchase at £85m – with the potential of a third arrival there and interest in Enzo Fernandez of Chelsea .

Bouaddi excelled in the World Cup for Morocco as a teenager and City see him as a talent with the ability to get better still.

Director of football Enzo Maresca said: "Ayyoub's potential is extremely high - a player equipped with everything a top midfielder needs.

"At just 18, he already has outstanding football intelligence and that will only improve under the guidance of Enzo [Maresca, the manager].

"We have watched him very, very closely and throughout that process we have become increasingly convinced he is a huge talent who will thrive at City."

Bouaddi, who was the youngest player in Lille's history, will be charged with replacing Rodri and Bernardo Silva , who have joined Barcelona and Real Madrid respectively.

City could lose four midfielders this summer, with Tijjani Reijnders moving to Al Qadsiah for £51m and Newcastle agreeing a £52m fee for Nico Gonzalez.

Bouaddi, who will take the No 32 shirt at City, said: "I am really, really happy – really proud to be here at one of the greatest clubs in the world.

"This is a very special day for me and my family. Manchester City are, for me, the best Club in the world. It's a dream to be here and be able to call myself a City player. I have spent most of my life working hard to become the best player I can be and reach the top of the game.

"I've watched City for many years, and I love their style of play. City always try and play quality football. And they have shown they are winners – this Club feels like it's built to win.

"The squad is world-class and Enzo is a top manager. And I'm really looking forward to playing at the Etihad Stadium, in front of all the fans.

"I think it was the right time because I was good in Lille, I felt very good, but I felt it was the right moment to step over and coming to City."

articles.title: Form the key in Swansea striker battle
articles.summary: Vitor Matos says his forwards will be judged purely on form as Zan Vipotnik, Adam Idah and Ross Stewart compete for game-time at Swansea City this season.  V...
articles.body:
Vitor Matos says his forwards will be judged purely on form as Zan Vipotnik , Adam Idah and Ross Stewart compete for game-time at Swansea City this season.

Vipotnik was the top scorer in the Championship in 2025-26, but his sparkling form last term did not save the Slovenia international from being left out of Matos' starting side in last weekend's draw with Sheffield United.

Vipotnik had begun Swansea's opening-day victory over Stoke City, but was substituted after a low-key display as Idah came on to Swansea's winner at the Bet365 Stadium.

Republic of Ireland international Idah was picked against the Blades and produced an effective display before Vipotnik and new recruit Ross Stewart featured as substitute.

"It's about performance, nothing more," said Swansea head coach Matos.

"That doesn't change for striker, midfielder or winger.

"Who we use, when they are all in shape and on their best moment , it will depend on the opposition. When one is in a better moment than the other, then it's about us taking the best of that one and then we keep moving, like in all the positions."

Questions remain over whether Vipotnik will still be a Swansea player after the transfer window closes next Tuesday.

Regardless of the transfer situation, Idah may be favourite to start at Derby County on Saturday given the solid shift he put in last time out.

"I think Adam gave us the physicality we knew we needed on that position because of the man marking and because of the one-v-one on the last line," Matos said.

"We didn't really connect the way we wanted to find him in the best moment, but he offered a lot.

"I think he was quite important to push the team to the opposition half and that's what we gained with him."
